data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik that has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of nine companies: one public (277810.KQ) and eight private-stage robotics firms including Humanoid, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value, applies a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next funding round, implying a valuation of $130M. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: Humanoid ($1.4B, Series A), Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), and Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B). The median across this set is $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce materially divergent results, reflecting the inherent dispersion in robotics valuations at this stage. Triangulation yields a low of $110M, median of $890M, and high of $1.9B. The wide range reflects uncertainty around whether Vulcan Elements will track toward the stage-progression trajectory or justify a peer-comparable valuation closer to the $1.4B–$1.8B band observed in recent Series A/B robotics fundings.
